TP53 mutation is a common genetic event in sporadic MBs and that TP53 mutations are frequently associated with CTNB1 mutation and/or MYCN amplification but do not have a negative impact on the clinical outcome of MB patients.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TP53 mutation is frequently observed in WNT MBs and is compatible with favorable prognosis.

The main takeaway from our work is that

TP53 mutation in sporadic MBs is not associated with poor prognosis and is compatible with favorable clinical outcome, but it is frequently associated with MYCN amplification, which is an adverse prognosticator.

in the majority of sporadic MB, p53 mutations occur late in the tumorigenic process, after MYCN amplification or CTNNB1 mutations have already occurred, and are compatible with long-term disease survival.
